claims.text: Applying surface mechanical attrition treatment (SMAT) to a metal substrate produces a gradient nanograined heterostructure.
A SMAT-produced gradient nanograined heterostructure concurrently enhances strength and ductility.
The initial metal may have a uniformly coarse-grained microstructure.
SMAT can induce a nanograined surface layer while retaining a coarser-grained core.
SMAT can be performed at ambient temperature and atmospheric pressure to create the proposed gradient structure.
Tuned SMAT processing parameters can create a gradient layer several microns thick.
The resulting graded microstructure consists of a fine nanograined surface layer and a coarse-grained interior.
Fine surface grains increase yield strength by impeding dislocation motion through the Hall–Petch effect.
The coarse-grained core permits enhanced plastic deformation and strain hardening.
Plastic deformation and strain hardening in the coarse-grained core improve ductility.
SMAT-treated samples will have higher yield strength than untreated coarse-grained samples.
SMAT-treated samples will have greater elongation than untreated coarse-grained samples.
The effectiveness of SMAT may be limited by the thickness and uniformity of the gradient layer.
The effectiveness of SMAT may vary with material composition and processing conditions.
